title: The Feeling of Being Trusted
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Starting from Warren Buffett's remark that he likes 'the feeling of being trusted,' the piece argues that many admired leaders build their lives around that feeling. Its claim is that leaders who covet being trusted work to behave in trustworthy ways, holding high personal standards and never negotiating their principles. The mechanism it names is consistency: congruence between actions and values, repeated day in and day out, produces the stability, reliability and predictability people respond to. When others can predict a leader's decisions from their values and past behavior, they extend trust. The piece closes by suggesting readers might enjoy the same feeling.
points: Buffett's quote is used to name a feeling many leaders value but rarely articulate, and which motivates trustworthy behavior.
Leaders who prize being trusted hold high personal standards and refuse to negotiate their principles.
Consistency is called the main ingredient of trust, requiring congruence between values and actions across engagement and decisions.
Predictability is the mechanism: when people can forecast a leader's decisions from their values and past actions, they extend trust.
quotes: Legendary investor Warren Buffett was recently asked why he still enjoyed investing money for others. He replied, “I like the feeling of being trusted.

That statement explains a lot about Buffet and captures a feeling many leaders value but rarely articulate. Many of the most admired leaders in the world build their lives and reputations around the feeling of being trusted.

Not surprisingly, when leaders covet being trusted, they work hard to act in trustworthy ways so they might soak in this feeling more frequently. They have high personal standards and values and live by them rigidly. They never negotiate the principles they believe in.
When a leader is successful, the feeling of being trusted is an enduring emotion. Earning the right to have people trust you is a day-in-and-day-out commitment. Consistency is the main ingredient.
To earn the faith of trust, leaders must be unusually consistent with how they act, engage, and decide. The congruency of their actions and values is paramount. They work hard to never slip up.

People resonate with that consistency and place a tremendous weight on the stability, reliability, and predictability it produces. As a hallmark of credibility, the routines and actions that showcase consistency create repeatable results.
